ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A large cube consists of 125 small black and white cubes, such that any two adjacent faces of the small cubes have different colors, the corner cubes being black. How many small black cubes are used?

Assign coordinates (i, j, k) to the small cubes, where i, j, k each range from 0 to 4. Adjacent cubes differ in exactly one coordinate, so their colors alternate according to the parity of i + j + k. method.method_draft: Interpret the large cube as a 5 by 5 by 5 grid because the text says it contains 125 small cubes. Read the image/text as showing a checkerboard coloring: neighboring small cubes that share a face have opposite colors, with corner cubes black. Assign coordinates (i,j,k) with i,j,k from 0 to 4. Because adjacent cubes differ in exactly one coordinate, their color alternates by the parity of i+j+k. Since a corner such as (0,0,0) is black, all cubes with even i+j+k are black. In a 5x5x5 grid, the parity classes differ by one because there are 125 total cubes, so the black class has ceil(125/2)=63 cubes.
